claims.text: High mixing entropy favors retention of a homogeneous multimetal solid solution.
Atomic-size mismatch among the constituent metals produces lattice strain and local lattice distortion.
Lattice strain caused by atomic-size mismatch promotes atomic diffusion and phase segregation at high temperature.
Small atomic-size mismatch corresponds to lower lattice strain.
At low lattice strain, mixing entropy stabilizes the solid solution as temperature increases.
Above a critical lattice-strain threshold at high temperature, atomic diffusion accelerates.
Accelerated diffusion leads to phase segregation or chemical ordering.
Phase segregation or ordering undermines structural and chemical homogeneity.
Nanoparticles with low atomic-size mismatch will remain uniform solid solutions throughout 473–1923 K.
Nanoparticles with higher atomic-size mismatch will exhibit detectable phase segregation near the upper end of 473–1923 K.
Retention of a uniform solid solution will produce consistent catalytic and thermoelectric properties.
High-temperature phase segregation will alter catalytic selectivity or thermoelectric performance.
Severe oxidation, strongly reactive species, or processing defects can dominate stability instead of atomic-size mismatch.
The comparison starts from nanoparticles that are homogeneous, equiatomic solid solutions without room-temperature phase segregation.
